ནང་དུ་བཞག་ལ །མཆོད་པ་རྣམས་ལ་དམིགས་ནས་ངག་ཏུ། ཨོཾ་བཛྲ་ཨ་མྲི་ཏ་ཀུནྜ་ལི་ཧ་ན་ཧ་ན་ཧཱུཾ་ཧཱུཾ་ཕཊ་སྭཱ་ཧཱ། ཨོཾ་སྭ་བྷཱ་ཝ་ཤུནྡྷ་སརྦ་དྷརྨ་སྭ་བྷ

གྲུབ་པའི་མཆོད་ཡོན ། ཞབས་བསིལ་། མེ་ཏོག ། བདུག་སྤོས ། སྣང་གསལ ། ཞལ་ཟས ། རོལ་མོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་མཆོད་རྫས་བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པ་

༄༅། །དེའི་དཔྲལ་བར་ཨོཾ།མགྲིན་པར་ཨཱཿ ཐུགས་ཀར་ཧཱུཾ། ཐུགས་ཀའི་ཧཱུཾ་ལས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས་ལྷོ་ཕྱོགས་པོ་ཏ་ལ་ནས་འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་དབང་ཕྱུག་ལ།སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་
སེམས་དཔའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་བསྐོར་བ་བཛྲ་ས་མཱ་ཛཿ ཛཿ ཧཱུཾ་བཾ་ཧོཿ གཉིས་སུ་མེད་པར་ཐིམ། སླར་ཡང་རང་གི་སྙིང་ཁ་ནས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས། དབང་གི་ལྷ་ཚོགས་བཛྲ་ས་མཱཾ་ཛཿ ཨོཾ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཏུ་མཾ་ཞེས་
གསོལ་བ་བཏབ་པས་དབང་གི་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། ཨོཾ་བཛྲི་བྷ་ཝ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥཱུཉ་ཧཱུཾ། ཞེས་གསུངས་ཤིང་བུམ་པའི་ཆུས་སྤྱི་བོ་ནས་དབང་བསྐུར། སྐུ་གང་དྲི་མ་དག །ཆུ་ལྷག་མ་ཡར་ལུད་པ་ལས། བླ་མའི་ངོ་བོ་འོད་
དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པས་དབུ་བརྒྱན། རང་གི་སྙིང་ཁར་ཟླ་བའི་སྟེང་དུ། ཧྲིཿ དཀར་པོའི་མཐར་གསང་སྔགས་ཡི་གེ་དྲུག་མས་བསྐོར་བ་ལས་འོད་འཕྲོས། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་བྱས། ཚུར་འདུས་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་སེམས་
ཀྱི་ཐུགས་རྗེའི་བྱིན་རླབས་བསྡུས་ནས་རང་ལ་ཐིམ་པས། རང་གི་རྒྱུད་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབས་པར་གྱུར། ཨོཾ་མ་ཎི་པདྨེ་ཧཱུཾ། ཅི་ནུས་ཟླས། ཨོཾ་ཨརྱ་ཨ་ཝ་ལོ་ཀི་ཏེ་ཤྭ་རཱ་ས་པཱ་རི་ཝ་ར་ཨརྒྷཾ། པཱ་དྱཾ། པུཥྤཾ། དྷུ་པཾ། ཨ་ལོ་ཀེ༑
གནྡྷེ༑ ནཻ་ཝི་དྱཾ༑ ཤཔྟ་པྲ་ཏིཙྪ་སྭཱ་ཧཱ། སྐྱོན་གྱིས་མ་གོས་སྐུ་མདོག་དཀར། །རྫོགས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་དབུ་ལ་བརྒྱན། །ཐུགས་རྗེའི་སྤྱན་གྱིས་འགྲོ་ལ་གཟིགས། །སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། །

Mantra
Salutations! This is the practice of the Hundred Offerings <term>torma</term> <gloss>ritual cakes</gloss> composed by the glorious Sakyapa <term>Ngagchang Ngagi Wangpo Kunga Rinchen</term> <gloss>the Mantradhara Lord of Speech Great Joy Jewel</gloss>.
May merit be obtained! May merit be obtained!
May merit be obtained! May merit be obtained! May merit be obtained! May the merit of life be obtained! May merit be obtained! Merit! Merit be obtained! Merit be obtained! Merit be obtained!
May merit be obtained! May merit be obtained!

<leaf-break/>

In front of where one sits, arrange five sets of offering plates on a suitable stand and prepare clean water. Place the <term>lha bshos</term> <gloss>deity food offering</gloss> inside the offering plate. Visualize the offerings and recite: <term>Om vajra amrita kundali hana hana hum hum phat svaha</term>. <term>Om svabhava shuddha sarva dharma svabhava shuddho ham</term>. From the state of emptiness, from the syllable <term>Om</term> appears a vast and wide precious vessel. Inside, from the melting of <term>Om</term>, appear divine substances: drinking water, water for the feet, flowers, incense, lamps, food, music, and so forth. Imagine these inconceivable offering substances filling the entire expanse of space. <term>Om argham padyam pushpe dhupe aloke gandhe naividye shapta ah hum</term>. <term>Om vajra dharma ranita praranita</term>.

<leaf-break/>

At the forehead of the deity is <term>Om</term>. At the throat is <term>Ah</term>. At the heart is <term>Hum</term>. From the <term>Hum</term> at the heart, light radiates, inviting the Noble Avalokiteshvara from Potala in the south, surrounded by a host of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. <term>Vajra samaja! Jah hum bam ho!</term> They dissolve non-dually into the deity. Again, light radiates from one's own heart, inviting the host of initiation deities. <term>Vajra samaja!</term> I pray: <term>Om abhishinchatu mam</term> <gloss>Please bestow the initiation upon me</gloss>. The initiation deities say: <term>Om vajri bhava abhishincha hum</term>. They bestow initiation by pouring water from the flask through the crown of the head. The body is filled, impurities are cleansed, and the excess water overflowing at the crown transforms into the crown ornament of Amitabha, who is the essence of the Guru. At one's own heart, upon a moon disc, is the white syllable <term>Hrih</term> surrounded by the six-syllable mantra. Light radiates from it, performing the benefit of sentient beings. It gathers back the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas' compassion and dissolves into oneself, whereby one's own being is blessed. Recite <term>Om mani padme hum</term> as much as possible. <term>Om arya avalokiteshvara saparivara argham padyam pushpam dhupam aloke gandhe naividyam shapta pratichcha svaha</term>. Unstained by faults, white in body, adorned with a Perfect Buddha on the crown, looking upon beings with eyes of compassion: I prostrate to Avalokiteshvara!

བཅས་པ་རྣམས་དང། དཔལ་ལྡན་དམག་གསོར་རྒྱལ་མོ་འཁོར་དང་བཅས་པ་རྣམས་དང། དཔལམགོན་གདོང་བཞི་དང། གཞན་ཡང་ལྷ་ཆེན་པོ་བརྒྱད། ཀླུ་ཆེན་པོ་བརྒྱད། ཕྱོགས་སྐྱོང་བཅུ། རྒྱལ་པོ་ཆེན་པོ་སྔོ་བཞི། གཟའ་
ཆེན་པོ་བརྒྱད། རྒྱུ་སྐར་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད། འཇིགས་བྱེད་ཆེན་པོ་དགུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དཔལ་གཙང་རིགས་ཀྱི་མགོན་པོ་བདུན་ཅུ་རྩ་ལྔ་འཁོར་དང་བཅས་པ་རྣམ་དང། བླ་མ་དམ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་དང་དམ་
ལ་བཏགས་ཤིང། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསྟན་པ་དང། རྡོ་རྗེ་གདན་གྱིས་གཙོ་བྱས་པའི་རྒྱ་གར་དང་བོད་ཀྱི་གཙུག་ལག་ཁང་དང། གདན་ས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་རྣམས་སྐྱོང་ཞིང་བསྟན་པ་ལ་མངོན་པར་དགའ་
བའི་ལྷ་ཀླུ་འབྱུང་པོའི་ཚོགས་རྣམས་ལ་འབུལ་ལོ། །སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསྟན་པ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་དར་ཞིང་རྒྱས་པ་དང། བསྟན་པའི་རྩ་ལག་དཔལ་ལྡན་བླ་མ་དམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་རྣམྶ
ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཚེ་དང། མཛད་པ་འཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་བར་ཆད་ཐམས་ཅད་ཞི་བ་དང། རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་བདག་ཅག་དཔོན་སློབ་ཡོན་མཆོད་འཁོར་དང་བཅས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྔོན་གྱི་ལམ་ལས་གྱུར་པ་དང། འཕྲལ་གྱི་རྐྱེན་ལས་གྱུར་

...together with their entourages; the glorious Queen of the Army <term>Magzor Gyalmo</term> with her entourage; the glorious Four-Faced Protector; and furthermore, the eight great gods, the eight great nagas, the ten guardians of the directions, the four great kings, the eight great planets, the twenty-eight constellations, the nine great terrifiers, and so forth—the seventy-five glorious protectors of the pure classes with their entourages; those who have been bound by the command and oath of the sacred Gurus; and the hosts of gods, nagas, and spirits who protect the temples and special seats of India and Tibet, foremost of which is Vajra Seat <note>Bodh Gaya</note>, and who delight in the teachings: I offer to you. May the precious teachings of the Buddha spread and increase. May all obstacles to the life and activities of the pillars of the teachings—the glorious sacred Gurus and authentic spiritual friends—be pacified. May all harms from humans and non-humans, caused by past karma or immediate conditions, to ourselves—the yogis, master, students, and patrons—be pacified. May all outer and inner obstacles to the practice of the sacred Dharma be pacified. May all favorable conditions—life, merit, glory, wealth, and excellent qualities—increase...

<leaf-break/>

...and I pray that you offer a pure and good aspiration for great goodness to arise. <note>Recite "By my intention," etc.</note> By offering this <term>torma</term> to the <term>shramanas</term> who possess clairvoyance and others, may words of truth be accomplished! To the gods who guard us beings and the deities born simultaneously with us; Vaishravana, Jambhala, Vasudhara, Ganapati, Aparajita, and the other hosts of <term>yaksha</term> wealth deities; and the host of deities who provide protection and guardianship: I offer to you. For me and all sentient beings, may there be no fear of disease, poverty, or lack, and please make life, glory, and wealth increase. To the simultaneously-born gods and the <term>yaksha</term> wealth deities, by offering this <term>torma</term>, may glory and wealth increase! Purify and cleanse. I prostrate to the Blessed One, the Tathagata, the Victorious One of Many Jewels! I prostrate to the Tathagata of Supreme Beautiful Form! I prostrate to the Tathagata of Infinite Gentle Body! I prostrate to the Tathagata who is Free from All Fear! <note>The offering and generosity verse is similar</note>. To the lords of the four continents of Jambudvipa, foremost of which is the Vajra Seat of India; particularly the twelve <term>Tenma</term> sisters who protect the land of Tibet; specifically the four districts of U and Tsang; and individually to the regions and lands...

<leaf-break/>

...the five sisters of the wilderness <term>Tseringma</term> with their entourage; the great <term>yaksha</term> leaders Samjnaya and Jaya; and the twenty-eight <term>yakshas</term> who guard the directions and intermediate directions; the thirty-two great <term>yakshas</term> with their entourages; the Five Hundred Mothers <term>Hariti</term>, and the hosts of wilderness-dwelling sisters: I offer to you. For me and all sentient beings, may your intentions to harm by stealing life, majesty, and luster be pacified. Particularly for us and our entourages, may all unfavorable factors for practicing the Dharma be pacified, and please ensure that all goals in accord with the Dharma are accomplished according to our wishes. ཕྱག་དང་པོ་གཉིས་ཐུགས་ཀར་ཐལ་མོར་སྦྱར་ནས།སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་མཛད་པར་བསྐུལ་བ།གཡས་གཉིས་པས་ཤེལ་དཀར་གྱི་འཕྲེང་བ་བརྒྱ་རྩ་
བརྒྱད་འཛིན་པ།གཡོན་གཉིས་པས་མེ་ཏོག་པདྨ་དཀར་པོའི་ཡུ་བ་བཟུང་སྙན་གྱི་ཐད་སོར་ཁ་ཕྱེ་བའི་སྟེང་ན་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་དབང་གི་རྒྱལ་པོས་མཚན་པ།ཞབས་རྡོ་རྗེའི་སྐྱིལ་མོ་ཀྲུང་གིས་བཞུགས་ཤིང་།
སྐུ་ལ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་དང་དར་སྣ་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་མཛེས་པ།བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་དང་མི་འབྲལ་བར་མཚོན་པའི་བརྡར།རི་དགས་ཀྲིཥྞ་ས་རིའི་པགས་པས་ནུ་མ་གཡོན་པར་བཀབ་པ།དབུ་སྐྲུ་ནག་པོ་རལ་པའི་ཐོར་ཅོག་ཅན།
དེའི་དཔྲལ་བར་ཨོཾ།མགྲིན་པར་ཨ།ཐུགས་ཀར་ཧཱུཾ།ཐུགས་ཀའི་ཧཱུཾ་ལས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས་ལྷོ་ཕྱོགས་པོ་ཏ་ལ་ནས་འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་དབང་ཕྱུག་ལ།སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་
བསྐོར་བ་བཛྲ་ས་མཱ་ཛཿཛཿཧཱུཾ་བཾ་ཧོཿགཉིས་སུ་མེད་བར་ཐིམ།སླར་ཡང་རང་གི་སྙིང་ཁ་ནས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས།དབང་གི་ལྷ་ཚོགས་བཛྲ་ས་མཱ་ཛཿཨོཾ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཏུ་མཾ་ཞེས་གསོལ་བ་བཏབ་པས་དབང་གི་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་
<leaf-break/>
འདུལ་དེ་ལ་དེར་སྟོན་པ། །བཙུན་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། །ཇོ་བོ་ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོས་བདག་དང་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་སྡིག་པ་དང་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱང་ཞིང་དག་པ་དང་། །
བྱམས་པ་དང་སྙིང་རྗེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་བཅོས་མ་མ་ཡིན་པ་རྒྱུད་ལ་སྐྱེ་བར་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབ་ཏུ་གསོལ། མྱུར་དུ་རྣམ་མཁྱེན་རྫོཊ་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཐོབ་པར་བྱིན་གྱི་བརླབ་ཏུ་གསོལ།
རང་གི་སྙིང་ཁ་ནས་འོད་འཕྲོས་པས་རང་བཞིན་གྱི་གནས་ནས་རྩ་བའི་བླ་མ་ཤཱཀྱ་ཐུབ་པའི་རྣམ་(པ)ཅན་ལ་འཇིག་རྟེན་དང་འཇིག་རྟེན་ལས་འདས་པའི་གཏོར་མགྲོན་གྱིས་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་བསྐོར་བ་མདུན་གྱི་ནཁར་ཨོཾ་བཛྲ
ས་མཱ་ཛཿམ་ལུས་སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་གྱི་མགོན་གྱུར་ཅིང་། །བདུད་སྡེའི་དཔུང་བཅས་མི་བཟད་འཇོམས་མཛད་ལྷ། །དངོས་རྣམས་མ་ལུས་ཇི་བཞིན་མཁྱེན་གྱུར་པའི། །བཅོམ་ལྡན་འཁོར་(བ)གནས་འདིར་གཤེགས
སུ་གསོལ། །ན་མོ་བདེ་གཤེགས་སྙིང་པོ་འགྲོ་ཀུན་ཡོངས་ལ་ཁྱབ། །སེམས་ནི་རྒྱ་ཆེན་མཆོག་ཏུ་རབ་བསྐྱེད་དེ། །འགྲོ་བ་འདི་དག་མ་ལུས་སངས་རྒྱས་རྒྱུ། །འདི་ན་སྣོར་མིན་སེམས་ཅན་གང་ཡང་མེད། །

<term>Om Svasti</term> <gloss>Om, may all be well</gloss>.
To the Diamond Holder <note>Vajradhara</note>, who gathers all the Buddhas of the three times; to <term>Avalokiteshvara</term>, who protects the sentient beings of the three realms; to <term>Manjushri</term>, who clears the darkness of the mind of the three worlds. I bow to the feet of the one who is the clear emanation of the three lineages.
Here, for the benefit of those with a beginner's mind, I shall briefly describe the sequence of the practice for offering the One Hundred Tormas <note>original: "gtor ma brgya rtsa"</note>. First, with clean torma dough, prepare one deity-food <note>original: "lha bshos"</note>, two <term>Dzamtorma</term> <gloss>tormas for Dzambhala</gloss>, and as many small pills <note>original: "ril bu"</note> as possible. Arrange the necessary implements like the flask <note>original: "bum pa"</note> and five sets of clean water offering bowls according to the oral lineage practice. Sit yourself on a comfortable cushion with a peaceful mind. In front of you, on a suitable platform, arrange the five sets of offering bowls with clean water. Place the deity-food inside the torma vessel. Directing your focus to the offerings, recite:
<term>Om Vajra Amrita Kundali Hana Hana Hum Hum Phat Swaha</term>. <term>Om Svabhava Shuddha Sarva Dharma Svabhava Shuddho Ham</term>. 
From the state of emptiness, within vast and spacious vessels made of jewels arising from <term>Om</term>, from the melting of <term>Om</term>...
<leaf-break/>
Join the first two hands at the heart in the prayer gesture, requesting all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to act for the benefit of sentient beings. The second right hand holds a crystal rosary of one hundred and eight beads. The second left hand holds the stem of a white lotus flower, which opens at the level of the ear; upon it is a jewel, the King of Power. He sits in the diamond cross-legged posture, his body beautified by various jewels and silks. As a symbol of never being separated from the mind of enlightenment, the left breast is covered with the skin of a <term>Krishnasara</term> deer. He has black hair tied in a topknot. At his forehead is <term>Om</term>, at his throat <term>Ah</term>, at his heart <term>Hum</term>. From the <term>Hum</term> at his heart, light radiates, inviting the Noble Lord Avalokiteshvara from the Potala in the south. Surrounded by the host of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, <term>Vajra Samajah Jah Hum Bam Ho</term>. They dissolve inseparably. Again, light radiates from one's own heart, inviting the host of initiation deities, <term>Vajra Samajah</term>. Requesting: "Om, may you bestow the initiation upon me." Thus, the initiation deities...
<leaf-break/>
...teaching this and that to those who are to be tamed. I prostrate to the venerable Avalokiteshvara. O Great Compassionate Lord, please bless me and all sentient beings so that all our sins and obscurations may be purified and cleansed. Please bless us so that love, compassion, and the non-artificial mind of enlightenment may be born in our continuums. Please bless us so that we may quickly obtain the precious state of the perfectly enlightened Buddha. 
From the light radiating from one's heart, the root Guru in the form of Shakyamuni Buddha is invited from the natural abode. Surrounded by the gathering of worldly and transcendental guests for the torma, he resides in the space in front: <term>Om Vajra Samajah</term>. 
"O Protector of all sentient beings without exception, the deity who destroys the unbearable hosts of Mara's army; you who know all things exactly as they are—Blessed One, please come to this place with your retinue." 
"Namoh, the essence of the Sugatas pervades all beings. Having generated the supreme, vast mind, all these beings are the cause of Buddhahood. There is no sentient being here who is not of that nature."

གྱུར་ཅིག །བགེགས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྒྱུད་ལ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་ནི་རིན་པོ་ཆེ། །མ་སྐྱེ་བ་རྣམས་སྐྱེ་གྱུར་ཅིག །སྐྱེས་པ་ཉམས་པ་མེད་པར་ཡང་། །གོང་ནས་གོང་དུ་འཕེལ་བར་ཤོག །བགེགས་རིགས་ལ་སོགས་གནོད་བྱེད་འཁོར་བཅས་ལ། །གཏོར་མ་བསྔོས་པས་
ཕན་སེམས་སྐྱེ་བར་ཤོག །འགྲོ་བ་རིགས་དྲུག །ལམ་རྒྱུད་ལྔ། སྐྱེ་གནས་རྣམ་པ་བཞིས་བསྡུས་པའི་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་སྦྱིན་ནོ། །རིགས་དྲུག་སོ་སོའི་ལན་ཆགས་དང་། བུ་ལོན་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱང་ཞིང་། རིགས་དྲུག་གི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མཐའ་
དག་དང་བྲལ་ཏེ། ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་རིམ་གྱིས་རྫོགས་ནས། མྱུར་དུ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཐོབ་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག །རིགས་དྲུག་ལམ་གྱིས་བསྡུས་པའི་སེམས་ཅན་ལ། །གཏོར་མ་སྦྱིན་པས་བདེ་སྐྱིད་ཐོབ་པར་ཤོག །
ཡི་དགས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་མོ་ཁལ་མེ་འབར་ས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཕྱིའི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཅན། ནང་གི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཅན། མེ་ལྕེའི་འཁོར་ལོ་ཅན། ཟས་སྐོམ་གྱི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཅན། མཁའ་ལ་རྒྱུ་བ་རླུང་ལ་གནས་པ། བྱིང་ལག་ནས་པ། ཁ་འཐོར་གྱི་ཚོགས་བཀྲེས་སྐོམ་དབུལ་འཕོང་གིས་
བསྡུས་པ་མཐའ་དག་ལ་སྦྱིན་ནོ། །སོ་སོའི་མདུན་དུ་ཟས་སྐོམ་བདུད་རྩིའི་ཆར་ཆེན་པོ་བབས་ནས། ལུས་དང་སེམས་ལ་བན་པ་དང་། བདེ་བར་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཅིང་ཆོམ་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག །སེར་སྣའི་སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་བྱང་ཞིང་། ཡི་དགས་ཀྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་དང་བྲལ་ཏེ་
<leaf-break/>
ལན་ཆགས་འཁྱེར་བར་ཤོག །མཐོ་སྲིད་པའི་རྩེ་མོ་ནས་དམའ་དམྱལ་ཁམས་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་ཡན་ཆད་དུ་ཁ་ཞེན་ཅིང་དབང་ཆུང་བ། གཏོར་མ་འདོད་དབང་ས་ཐོབ་པ། མ་སླེབས་པ། གློ་བུར་ལྷགས་པའི་འགྲོན་སྐལ་བ་ཆད་པ། ཞ་བོ། ལོངས་པ། །
འོན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་སྐལ་ཆ་དབང་ཆུང་གི་རིགས། ལྷག་མ་དང་ཤལ་ཤུལ་ཟླ་བང་བ་རྣམས་ལ་སྦྱིན་ནོ། །སོ་སོའི་མདུད་དུ་ཟས་སྐོམ་བདུད་རྩིའི་ཆ་ར་ཆེན་པོ་བབས་ནས། ལུས དང་སེམས་ལ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མེད་ཅིང་། སོ་སོར་ཚེམ་ཞིང་དབང་
དུ་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ནས་མྱུར་དུ་རྣམ་མཁྱེན་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཐོབ་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག །ཁམས་གང་ན་མཁའ་ལ་མཛོད་པ་བཞིན་དུ། ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཟད་པ་མེད་པར་ཤོག །རྩོད་པ་མེད་ཅིང་ཚིམ་བགྱིས་ལ། །རང་དབང་
དུ་ཡང་སྤྱོད་པར་ཤོག །མ་དང་ད་ནང་ཤི་བ་བསད་པ་གཡང་ལ་ལྷུང་བ། ཚེ་འདིའི་སྣང་བ་ནུབ་ལ་ཕྱི་མ་རྩྭ་ལྟ་བ་མ་ཤར་བ། སྲིད་པ་བར་དོར་འཁྱམས་པའི་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་སྦྱིན་ནོ། །བར་དོ་ལ་བར་དོ་ངོས་ནས་
བར་དོ་འཇིགས་པའི་དགྲ་བཞི། ཉམས་ང་བའི་གཡང་ས་གསུམ། མ་ངེས་པའི་རྟགས་དྲུག་ལ་སོགས་པ་བར་དོ། །རྩྭ་ལྟ་བ། སྲིད་པའི་སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་གྲོལ་ཏེ། བར་དོར་རྒྱལ་བ་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་མངོན་དུ་བྱེད་པའི་སྐལ་བ་
<leaf-break/>
ལས་ཁྱད་ཀྱིས་སེམས་ཅན་དོན་ཀུན་མཛད། རྗེས་སུ་མཐུན་པའི་དངོས་གྲུབ་སྩོལ། །སངས་རྒྱས་ཡུལ་དུ་གཤེགས་ནས་ཀྱང་། སླར་ཡང་འབྱོན་པ། མཛོད་དུ་གསོལ། །བཛྲ་མུཿ མཆོད་སྦྱིན་གནས་འདིར་གང་ལྷགས་པ། འབྱུང་པོ་ལ་འོག་རྒྱུ་བ་
དང་། གང་དག་ས་སྟེང་འཁོད་དང་། ས་བླར་རྒྱུ་བ་གང་ཡིན་པ། འགྱུ་བར་བགྱིས་ལ་རང་གནས་སུ། ཐམས་ཅད་ཐ་དད་པར་གྲྭ་བར་གྱིས། སརྦ་ཐུ་ཏ་གཙྪ་པྲེ་ཁ་ཀཙྪ། བསོད་ནམས་འདི་ཡིས་ཐམས་ཅད་གཟིགས་པ་ཉིད། ཐོབ་ནས་ཉེས་པའི་དགྲ་རྣམས་
པས་བྱས་ཏེ། སྐྱེ་རྒ་ན་འཆིའི་རྦ་ཀློང་འཁྲུགས་པ་ཡི། སྲིད་པའི་མཚོ་ལས་འགྲོ་བ་བློ་ལ་བར་ཤོག །སྦྱིན་པ་འདི་ཡི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱིས། །སངས་རྒྱས་བསྟན་ལ་དད་གྱུར་པའི། །དགའ་བོ་ཉི་དགའ་ལ་སོགས་པ། །གཉུག་མར་གནས་པའི་ལྷ་ནས་དང་། །
རྒྱལ་པོ་སྦྱིན་བདག་ཉིད་དང་ནི། །གཞན་ཡང་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་གནས་པ་སོགས། །ཚེ་རིང་ནད་མེད་དུ་ན་སུམ་ཚོགས། །རྟག་ཏུ་བདེ་བ་ཐོབ་པར་ཤོག །བླ་མེད་བླ་མའི་ཐུགས་རྗེ་དང་། །རྒྱལ་དང་རྒྱལ་སྲས་རང་རྒྱལ་དང་། །དགྲ་བཅོམ་བདེན་པའི་བྱིན་རླབས་སྙིང་། །
དེ་ལྟར་བསྔོས་བཞིན་འགྲུབ་པར་ཤོག །སྟོན་མཆོག་དམ་པ་སོགས་བཀྲ་ཤིས་ཀྱི་ཚིག་ཇི་ལྟར་རིགས་པ་བརྗོད། །

"...may it be so! In the stream of being of the obstructing spirits, may the precious mind of enlightenment be born in those in whom it has not been born; in those where it has been born, may it not decline but increase further and further. 
By dedicating the torma to the classes of obstructing spirits and their harmful retinues, may a mind of benefit be born! 
I give this to all sentient beings included in the six classes of wanderers, the five paths, and the four types of birth. 
May all the karmic debts and loans of each of the six classes be purified, and being freed from all the sufferings of the six classes, and having gradually completed the six perfections, may they quickly attain the precious state of unsurpassed perfect Buddhahood. 
By giving the torma to the sentient beings included in the paths of the six classes, may they attain happiness! 
I give this to the host of hungry ghosts who are gathered by hunger, thirst, and poverty: those with outer obscurations like the Queen of Hungry Ghosts Jvalamukhi, those with inner obscurations, those with the wheel of flaming tongues, those with obscurations to food and drink, those who move in the sky, those who reside in the air, those who reside in the depths, and the scattered ones. 
May a great rain of nectar of food and drink fall before each of them, and being beneficial to their bodies and minds, may they enjoy it happily and be satisfied. 
May the sins and obscurations of stinginess be purified, and being freed from the suffering of hungry ghosts..."

<leaf-break/>

"...may their karmic debts be cleared! To those who are weak in speech and power from the peak of existence above down to the eighteen hell realms below, those who have the power to desire the torma but have not reached it, those guests who have suddenly arrived and whose share has been cut off, the lame, the blind, the deaf, and so forth—the classes of weak power and share—and to those who receive the leftovers and the remains, I give. 
May a great rain of nectar of food and drink fall before each of them, and being without suffering in body and mind, and being each satisfied and enjoying power, may they quickly attain the precious state of the omniscient perfect Buddha. 
May their wealth be inexhaustible, just like the 'Treasury of Space' in any realm. 
Without conflict and being satisfied, may they enjoy it independently! 
I give this to all sentient beings who died this morning or last night, those who were killed, those who fell down a cliff, those for whom the light of this life has set and the light of the next has not yet dawned, and those who wander in the intermediate state <note>bardo</note> of existence. 
Regarding the intermediate state, may they be freed from the four terrifying enemies of the bardo, the three dangerous cliffs, the six uncertain signs, and all the sins and obscurations of existence, and in the bardo, may they possess the fortune of...

<leaf-break/>

...specifically, may you perform all the goals of sentient beings and bestow corresponding accomplishments. 
Even after you have gone to the Buddha-field, please come again! 
<term>Vajra Muh</term>. 
Whoever has arrived at this place of offering and charity, whether they are spirits who move below the earth, or those who reside on the earth, or those who move above the earth: having moved, please return to your own places, each to your own separate quarters. 
<term>Sarva Bhuta Gachha Prekha Gachha</term>. 
By this merit, may all beings attain the state of seeing everything, and having defeated the enemies of faults, may they be delivered from the ocean of existence, which is turbulent with the waves of birth, aging, sickness, and death. 
By the merit of this generosity, may the indigenous deities led by Ananda and Sunanda, who have faith in the Buddha's teachings, and the kings who are patrons, and others residing in cities and so forth, have long lives, no disease, and perfect prosperity, and may they always attain happiness. 
By the compassion of the unsurpassed Gurus, and the blessing of the truth of the Victors, the Sons of the Victors, the Solitary Realizers, and the Arhats, may it be accomplished just as dedicated. 
Recite appropriate auspicious verses like "The Supreme Teacher," etc.

ཐབས་དང་འབྲེལ་བར་དབང་བསྐུར་བ་ལ་གསུམ་སྟེ ། སྦྱོར་བ་ཡོ་བྱད་ཀྱི་བཤམས ། དངོས་གཞི་སྒྲུབ་པའི་ཐབས ། བྱིན་རླབས་དབང་གི་ཆོ་གའོ ། ། དང་པོ་ཡོ་བྱད་བཤམས་པ་ནི ། སྟེགས་བུའི་ཁར་མེ་ཏོག་གི་ཚོམ་བུའི་སྟེང་དུ་མཉྫིཿལ་ཚེ་འབྲང་བུམ་གཟུགས་
རྟ་མགོས་མཚན་པ་བཞག ། དེའི་གཡས་སུ་ཚེ་རིལ ། གཡོན་དུ་ཚེ་ཆང་། མདུན་དུ་གཏོར་ཟླུམ་གཉིས་དང་། མཆོད་ཡོན་སྔོན་འགྲོའི་ཉེར་སྤྱོད་རྣམས་བཤམས ། གཞན་ཡང་རྡོར་དྲིལ་མེ་ཏོག་སྔོན་གཏོར་སོགས་ཉེ་བར་མཁོ་བའི་ཡོ་བྱད་རྣམས་ཚོགས་
པར་བྱའོ ། ། གཉིས་པ་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་ལ ། བགེགས་བསྐྲད ། མཚམས་བཅད ། སྐྱབས་སེམས་སྔོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བས ། རང་གི་སྙིང་གའི་ཧྲཱིཿལས་འོད་ཟེར་འཕྲོས་པས་བླ་མ་དཔག་མེད་ལ་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་བསྐོར་བ་
བཛྲ་ས་མཱ་ཛཿ ས་སྤྱན་དྲངས ། ཨརྒྷཾ་ནས་ཤཔྟའི་བར་གྱིས་མཆོད ། དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ལ་བདག་སྐྱབས་འཆི ། ། སོགས་ཀྱིས་རྒྱུན་བཤགས་དང་ཚད་མེད་བཞི་སྒོམ ། དངོས་གཞི་ནི ། སྭ་བྷ་ཝས་སྦྱངས ། སྟོང་པའི་ངང་ལས་གཞལ་ཡས་ཁང་བདེ་

# Om Svasti
I bow to the Vajra of Speech, Amitabha <note>Buddha of Boundless Light</note>, who bestows the supreme deathless state out of affection for beings; I shall now explain a brief method for his accomplishment. 

Regarding the empowerment related to the practice known as "Bestowing the Splendor of Deathlessness," there are three parts: the preparatory arrangement of materials, the main practice method, and the ritual ceremony of the blessing empowerment. 

First, the arrangement: Upon a platform, on a heap of flowers, place a longevity torma in the shape of a vase marked with a horse's head upon a pedestal. To its right, place longevity pills; to its left, longevity wine. In front, place two circular tormas and the preliminary offering materials. Furthermore, gather necessary implements like the vajra, bell, flowers, and the preceding torma. 

Second, for the practice method: Expel obstructing spirits and establish the boundary. Preceded by refuge and bodhicitta, light rays radiate from the HRIH at one's heart, inviting the Boundless Master surrounded by the assembly of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with <term>Vajra Samaja</term>. Make offerings from <term>Argham</term> to <term>Shapta</term>. 

"I take refuge in the Three Jewels..." perform the daily confession and meditate on the Four Immeasurables. For the main practice: purify with the <term>Svabhava</term> mantra. From within the state of emptiness, in the center of the perfectly complete realm of Sukhavati <note>The Blissful Pure Land</note>, upon a precious throne raised by lions and a seat of lotus and moon, from the HRIH syllable, one arises as the Protector Amitayus, red in color, with one face and two hands, in a peaceful and smiling mood. 

<leaf-break/>

# Glorious Sonam Chokden! 
At the feet of the matchless kindness, the Spontaneous Activity <note>Trinley Lhundrup</note>, to the supreme masters of the root and lineage, I pray! Bestow your blessings! If there are other specific lineage variations, they may be added as desired, but in any case, by praying thus, light rays radiate from the bodies of those lineage Knowledge-Holders <note>term: "Vidyadhara"</note>. 

Imagine that one's own life-force and life-span, which may have wandered, scattered, or declined, along with all the qualities of the environment and inhabitants of cyclic existence and transcendence, are drawn in as the essence of nectar and dissolve into the masters at the crown of one's head. From their bodies, a stream of deathless nectar flows down, entering through the crown of oneself, clearly visualized as Amitayus. Imagine that the whole body is filled and the accomplishment of deathless life is obtained. 

Recite: <term>Om Ah Hum Hrih Hrih Vajra Guru Padma Siddhi Punya Jnana Ayu Siddhi Hum Dza</term> hundreds or thousands of times. The benchmark for the retreat is one million recitations. 

When concluding the session, again with intense devotion: "O root and lineage masters and gathered deities of the Yidam, increase your compassionate power, strength, and support! Pacify illnesses, spirits, adverse conditions, and obstacles, and please bestow the accomplishment of deathless life!" 

By praying thus, the lineage masters at the crown dissolve into light in sequence and enter through one's crown, dissolving into the HRIH at the heart. Think that the accomplishment of deathless life is obtained. Finally, even oneself is dissolved into the HRIH at the heart, and one rests in the natural state of deathless suchness.

<leaf-break/>

# Known as the King...
The great Accomplished One <note>Siddha</note> who directly realized the natural state of the profound Dharmata, who saw the faces of many supreme Yidam deities, and who performed great benefit for beings by gaining mastery over the four types of activity: he went in his actual body to the palace of Lotus Light in the Southwest continent of Chamara and heard infinite profound and vast instructions from the Great One of Uddiyana <note>Padmasambhava</note>. 

In particular, he heard this profound longevity practice, which later also emerged from the profound treasures of Chimpü, becoming like the merging of two rivers. By practicing this himself, the Great Siddha lived for about one hundred and twenty-five years. Many of his followers also lived for over a hundred years. As a sign of its potency and blessing, which is superior to others, the empowerment is given through this practice known as "Bestowing the Splendor of Deathlessness." 

The actions of the Master have already been completed. Now, please offer a mandala as payment for requesting the profound empowerment which is your share. Having offered the mandala, repeat these words of prayer: 

"O Great Joy, you are my teacher; Master, please think of me! To the one who shows the way of Great Enlightenment, the Great Protector, I seek your guidance. Bestow upon me that very samaya <note>sacred bond</note>. Bestow upon me the heart of enlightenment. The Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—bestow these three refuges upon me. Into the supreme city of Great Liberation, O Protector, [lead] me..."

དུ་གནས་ཤིང་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ཡོངས་ཀྱི་བསྲུང་མ། ཁྱད་པར་དུར་ཁྲོད་ཆེན་པོ་བསིལ་བའི་ཚལ་དུ་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཁའ་འགྲོ་སེང་གེའི་གདོང་པ་ཅན་གྱིས་བསྟན་པ་བསྲུང་བར་དབང་བསྐུར་ཞིང་འཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་གཉེར་གཏད། སླར་ཡང་བལ་བོད་ཀྱི་སོ་མཚམས་ཁ་ལ་རོང་སྒོ་ལ་སོགས་པར་སློབ་དཔོན་
ཆེན་པོ་པདྨ་འབྱུང་གནས་ཀྱིས་དམ་ལ་བཏགས་ཤིང་ལྟ་ལོག་མུ་སྟེགས་ཀྱི་རྒོལ་བ་བསྲུང་བ་སོགས་བོད་ཁམས་བདེ་སྐྱིད་ཀྱི་དཔལ་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པས་སྐྱོང་བར་བཀའ་བསྒོས་ཤིང་རང་གིས་ཁས་བླང་དམ་བཅས་པ་ལྟར། སྤྱིར་བོད་ཁམས་སྡེ་དང་བཅས་པ་མཐའ་དག་དང་། ཁྱད་པར་གསང་
ཆེན་བསྟན་པའི་སྙིང་པོ་དེ་འཛིན་དང་བཅས་པ་གཅེས་པའི་བུ་བཞིན་དུ་སྐྱོང་ཞིང་འཕྲིན་ལས་རྣམ་པ་བཞི་ལ་ཐོགས་པ་མེད་པའི་མཐུ་ཅན། ནང་དུ་སྙིང་ཉེ་ལ་བཀྲ་ཤིས་པ། ཕྱི་རུ་རྣོ་མྱུར་ཚན་ཆེ་བ། རིག་འཛིན་སྒྲུབ་པ་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རེ་བ་ཡིད་བཞིན་དུ་བསྐོང་བའི་དབང་གི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལྟ་བུ་འདི་ལ། བརྟན་
མ་ལས་རྒྱ་མཚོའི་རྒྱུད་དང་བསྙེན་སྒྲུབ་མཆོད་སྐོངས་ལས་ཕྲན་སོགས་གདམས་པའི་བཀའ་སྲོལ་ཇི་སྙེད་ཅིག་མཆིས་པ་ལས། གཙོ་བོར་གྱུར་པ་ནི་བླ་མ་མངའ་བདག་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ཆོས་དབང་རིན་པོ་ཆེས་གཏེར་ནས་སྤྱན་དྲངས་པ་ལས་སྲོག་གཏད་ཀྱི་བཀའ་ནི་གཏེར་ཁ་འོག་མ་ལས་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ཅིང་།
དེ་ཉིད་རིག་འཛིན་བརྒྱུད་པའི་ཕྱག་བཞེས་བཞིན་སྒྲུབ་པ་ལ་སློབ་དཔོན་གྱི་བྱ་བ་རྣམས་སྔོན་དུ་གྲུབ། སློབ་མའི་བྱ་བ་མཎྜལ་ཕུལ་ནས་གསོལ་བ་གདབ་པ། ཨེ་མ་ཧོ། མ་ཧཱ་གུ་རུ་རྡོ་རྗེ་འཛིན། །སངས་རྒྱས་བསྟན་པ་བསྲུང་བ་དང་། །ཇི་ལྟར་འདོད་པའི་དོན་སྒྲུབ་པ། །མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་མོ་
བརྟན་མའི་ཚོགས། །སྙིང་ཉེའི་གྲོགས་སུ་བདག་ལ་སྩོལ། །ཅེས་ལན་གསུམ། སློབ་དཔོན་གྱིས། ཨེ་མ་ཧོ། སྔོན་གྱི་བསྐལ་པ་དང་པོ་ལ། །འཇིགས་བྱེད་རྡོ་རྗེ་སྲིན་པོ་ཡིས། །བཀའ་སྩལ་ཇི་བཞིན་ཉེར་བླངས་ནས། །བསྟན་པ་བསྲུང་བ་བརྟན་མའི་ཚོགས། །

Om Svasti! The secret of the speech of all Buddhas appears in the form of the Vajra Master. Bowing to him, I shall briefly explain the practice of the Tenma <note>Twelve Tenma Goddesses</note> who are bound by oath. Here, regarding the life-entrustment associated with the practice of the Twelve Tenma Sisters, the protectors of Tibet, who appear in the treasure of Chowang, there are three parts: the preparation of the ritual implements, the main practice method, and the stages of the life-entrustment.

First, the preparation: At a special time in a solitary place, display the Tutelary Deity and, if available, a painted image of these goddesses. In front, on a suitable platform, draw a mandala with twelve lotus petals and a perimeter, or use a white cloth base with heaps of white rice placed at the locations of each deity. In the center, on a small stand, place the <term>torma</term> of the "overpowering" tutelary deity, such as the peaceful or wrathful Guru, adorned with a symbolic image and a silk-bound arrow. On the twelve petals, starting from the east: for the four demonesses, four black triangular cakes; for the four <term>yakshis</term>, four red rectangular cakes with rounded tops; for the four <term>menmo</term> <gloss>medicinal goddesses</gloss>, four white round cakes. Adorn each with its respective symbolic image and silk streamers. In front of these, on a skin of a wild animal or a "vow-violator," place a "lotus-protecting" offering cake, or twelve round cakes adorned with various excellent foods. On the right, place medicinal libations; on the left, blood. Prepare "flour-butter" offerings in Chinese or silver bowls, first-portion drinks with grain and gold/turquoise, "white drink" of milk and medicine, and "sweet drink" of honey-wine and molasses. Gather the five standard offerings, clouds of smoke from medicinal wood and frankincense, silk-bound arrows, various ornaments, and all other necessary items.

Second, the practice method: Begin with the self-generation yoga and recitation of the "overpowering" deity. Bless the offerings, especially sprinkling the <term>torma</term> with medicinal libations. Recite: **Om Ah Hum Tram Spharana Phat Samharana Hum Tram Ratna Trailokya Phat.** By saying this, each atom of the <term>torma</term> becomes a jewel tent of inexhaustible enjoyments, filling the sky.

<leaf-break/>

To the Twelve Tenma Sisters who guard the land of Tibet, the Great Master Padmasambhava gave individual names, ornaments, attire, and mounts, and appointed them as guardians of the teachings. Remembering your former heart-pledges and oaths of love, come here with your many attendants and servants! With your many fluttering jewel ornaments, come here, fulfill your oaths, and accept this sacrificial <term>torma</term>! Twelve Tenma Sisters who guard the land of Tibet, remember your former oaths! Having accepted this offering of medicine, blood, and <term>torma</term>, cause the entire teaching of the Buddha to flourish! Fulfill the intentions of me, the practitioner!

Thus, make the request. Visualize that light rays from one's own heart incite the oath-bound ones and their retinue. Remembering their former oaths, they perform activities. Recite: **Vajra Arali Jah Vajra Arali Hum. Vajra Titi Dhe. Vajra Bhara Dha. Vajra Sabya Hum. Vajra Titi Hum. Vajra Mati Hum. Vajra Tide Sa Hum. Vajra Kharali Hum. Vajra Sing So Hum. Vajra Yaksha Phyir. Vajra Du Phyir Saran Phat. Ma Dung Bhyo Ma Dung Bhyo. Hum Hum Jah Jah.** Many variations of the mantra suffixes for requesting accomplishments or for fierce actions are taught, but for this occasion, it is sufficient to recite the above. Finally, sprinkle the <term>torma</term> with meat, butter, wine, and nectar. Bless it with **Om Ah Hum**. Offer it three times with: **...So Vajra Yaksha Krota Hum. Mama. Kha Kha. La La. Le Le. Ta Ta. Te Te. Kharakma.** etc.

**Hum!** I am Padmasambhava! At Palmo Palthang in Upper Tsang, at the base of the divine lake and the demoness lake, I bound you by oath, you hosts of Tenma! Some are black, the hosts of demonesses; some are red, the hosts of <term>yakshis</term>; some are white, of beautiful form; some are blue, of the form of the sky. You twelve great <term>mamos</term> are the great land-owners of Tibet! You hosts of Tenma bound by oath, do not allow false Dharma or the extremist views of the non-Buddhists into Tibet—protect it! Do not cause obstacles to the practitioners of the Secret Mantra—protect them! You who bless the great sacred sites—

<leaf-break/>

—following an appropriate introduction: In the ultimate sense, they reside as the <term>dakinis</term> of the expanse of primordial wisdom. In appearance, they are the <term>mamos</term> of the oath. Manifesting as messengers of swift activity, they are known as the Twelve Tenma Sisters. Ultimately, they reside within the retinue of the Great Glorious Heruka and are the protectors of the entire mandala. Specifically, in the great charnel ground of Cool Grove, the Wisdom Dakini Simhamukha <gloss>Lion-Faced One</gloss> empowered them to protect the teachings and entrusted them with activities. Later, at the border of Nepal and Tibet, at Khala Rong-go and elsewhere, the Great Master Padmasambhava bound them by oath. He commanded them to guard against the attacks of non-Buddhists with wrong views and to protect the land of Tibet with the excellence of peace and happiness. Just as they promised and swore, they guard all of Tibet and its regions, and specifically, they cherish the essence of the Great Secret teachings and its holders like their own children. They possess the power to act without hindrance in the four activities. Internally kind and auspicious, externally sharp, swift, and powerful, they are like a King of Power who fulfills the hopes of the Knowledge-Holder practitioners. 

Many traditions of instructions exist, such as the "Tantra of the Ocean of Tenma Activities," and various rituals of approach, accomplishment, offering, and fulfillment. The primary ones are those invited from treasure by the Great Sovereign Master <note>Nyang Ralpa</note> and the Precious Guru Chowang. The life-entrustment command comes from the "Later Treasure." Performing it according to the practice of the Knowledge-Holder lineage, the teacher's preliminary actions are completed. The student offers a mandala and makes the request: "Emaho! Great Guru, Vajra Holder! For the protection of the Buddha's teachings and the accomplishment of desired goals, please grant the hosts of Tenma Dakinis and Mamos to me as kind-hearted friends!" Request thus three times. 

The Master says: "Emaho! In the first eon of the past, the Terrifying Vajra Rakshasa <note>referring to a wrathful deity form</note> gave his command, which you accepted. You hosts of Tenma who protect the teachings!"

༄༅། །ཨོཾ་སྭསྟི། གསང་བདག་དཔའ་བོ་རྡོ་རྗེ་འཛིན། །མཐུ་ཆེན་དྲེགས་པའི་སྐུར་བཞེངས་ནས། །གདུག་པ་འདུལ་མཛད་རྭ་ཧུ་སར། །བཏུད་ནས་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་དབང་ཆོག་བཤད། །འདིར་གཟའ་བདུད་ཆེན་པོ་རཱ་ཧུ་སའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས།
དང་འབྲེལ་བར་དབང་བསྐུར་བ་ལ་གསུམ་སྟེ། སྦྱོར་བ་ཡོ་བྱད་ཀྱི་གཤོམས། དངོས་གཞི་སྒྲུབ་པའི་ཐབས་དང་། དབང་གི་ཆོ་གའོ། དང་པོ་ཡོ་བྱད་བཤམ་པ་ནི། འགྱུ་དུས་བརྒྱད་སོགས་དུས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་ལ། གནས་དབེན་པར་བྲིས་སྐུ་བཀྲམ་པའི་མདུན་དུ།
སྟེགས་བུའི་ཁར་མཎྜལ་སྒོ་རྫོགས་ལྟེ་བར་པདྨ་འདབ་བརྒྱད་དང་ཁྱམས་ཤར་ནས་བརྩམས་ཏེ་སྔོ་སེར་དམར་ལྗང་དུ་བྱས་པའི་ལྟེ་བར་གཙོ་བོ་དང་། འདབ་མ་བརྒྱད་ལ་གཟའ་བརྒྱད། ཁྱམས་ལ་རྒྱུ་སྐར་ཉེར་བརྒྱད། སྒོ་བཞིར་གདོང་མོ་བཞི་རྣམས་ས་བོན་ནམ་

དཔུང་སྡང་མིག་གིས། །དགྲ་དང་བགེགས་ལ་འབྲུ་ཚུགས་བལྟ། །སྐུ་སྨད་ས་ལ་བརྡབས་པ་ཡིས། །འཇིག་རྟེན་གཡོ་འགུལ་འདེག་པར་བྱེད། །ཞལ་ནས་ཧཱུྃ་དང་ཕཊ་སྒྲོག་པས། །དྲེགས་པ་ཕོ་མོ་དབང་དུ་སྡུད། །སྐུ་མདོག་དུད་ཁ་འཇིགས་པ་ཡིས། །

# Om Svasti!
The Lord of Secrets, the Hero, the Holder of the Vajra,
Having arisen in the form of a great powerful and arrogant one,
The subduer of the wicked, Rahula;
Bowing to him, I shall explain the practice method and empowerment ritual.

Herein lies the practice method of the Great Planetary Demon Rahula <note>The text uses the transliteration Rahusa/Rahu-sa</note> and its associated empowerment, which consists of three parts: the preparation of ritual materials, the main practice method, and the ritual of empowerment.

Regarding the first part, the preparation of materials: On special occasions such as the eight astrological junctions <note>Eight major divisions of the lunar month</note>, in a solitary place, set out a painted scroll. In front of it, on a platform, prepare a complete mandala. At the center, draw an eight-petaled lotus with a courtyard, starting from the east and colored blue, yellow, red, and green. In the center, place the main deity. On the eight petals, place the eight planets. In the courtyard, place the twenty-eight constellations. At the four gates, place the four Face-Daughters <note>Female guardian deities with animal faces</note>, represented by seeds or heaps of grain. In the center, on a tripod, place a vase filled with nectar and fully adorned. In front, place the empowerment ritual cake <gloss>torma</gloss>, triangular and encircled by eight similar ritual cakes, adorned with red ornaments. Insert a black arrow with silk streamers and a ritual card <term>tsakli</term>. To its right and left, place the medicinal medicine <gloss>amrita</gloss> and blood <gloss>rakta</gloss>. To the south, place the four implements of the main deity and a ritual card of a fire-mound. To the north, place the images and implements of the eight planetary attendants. To the west, arrange the offering tormas. Surround the edges with the five common offerings. Furthermore, gather all other necessary materials below.

Regarding the second part, the practice method: Precede this with the meditation and recitation of any of one's own wrathful Tutelary Deities, such as the Lord of Secrets. Then, bless the general and special offerings. Purify the support in front. Out of emptiness comes a Hum syllable, which transforms into a protection circle surrounded by a terrifying great charnel ground. In the center, amidst churning waves of blood and fat, from the letter E, arises a dark blue triangular space equal to the sky. In its center, on a lotus, sun, and seat of enemies and obstructors, is a particle of dark yellow color...

<leaf-break/>

...the Great One, yellow-black, holding a snake-noose and a crocodile. The army of Naga-Demons... In the northeast is Sha, Rahu, smoke-colored, holding a crocodile and a tally-stick, surrounded by the army of the eight classes of gods and spirits. All are fierce and wrathful, having the form of Rakshasas with nine heads. Their entire bodies are covered in eyes, possessing a terrifying appearance similar to the main deity. Outside that, in the east, from Ma, is the Tiger-Existence with a sickle face, white-yellow, holding a hook and a noose. In the south, from Ra, is the Bam-Existence with a brown bear face, yellow-black, holding a skull-club and a snake-noose. In the west, from Tsa, is the Kong-Existence with an ox face, red-black, holding a battle-axe and a noose. In the north, from Sha, is the Nomad-Existence with a crocodile face, green-black, encircling the base of Mount Meru. All four have the appearance of wrathful Rakshasi goddesses, seated on seats of human skin. Furthermore, outside of these are the seventy-five Lords of the Pure Lineage and an inconceivable host of spirits of the three worlds. All are wrathful and fierce, devouring and roaring, jumping and running, possessing the skill of great swift miraculous power, dwelling in the midst of the churning fire and wind of the end of the age.

On their foreheads is Om, at their throats is Ah, at their hearts is Hum. From the Hum, rays of light radiate, and from their natural dwelling places, the Great Planetary Demon and his retinue are invited. Think thus:

Hum! From the heart emanation of the Vajra Holder,
You manifest as a terrifying, blazing body of further emanation;
Great powerful Rahula, the terrifying subduer!
Though you do not move from the state of the sphere of reality,
In this final five-hundred-year era of the degenerate age,
To subdue the wicked through various means,
Though your heart is peaceful in the pure sphere of reality,
Arise in a fierce, terrifying, and blazing body!
From the blazing mandala of hatred and desire,
The power...

<leaf-break/>

...it is also acceptable to use these two verses. If you wish to expand:

Hrih! Great Vishnu, Rahu the Seizer,
In the blazing expanse of your terrifying body;
With nine faces and four arms, you are majestic,
Possessing fierce skill across the world realms!
Lord of the meteor of sky-iron,
Chief who brings down the hail of the storm!
Great emanation possessing miraculous powers,
Chief of the gods atop Mount Meru!
Lord of the Nagas at the bottom of the ocean!
Master of the eight classes in the atmosphere!
With nine heads, you are the lord of the three existences!
One head is the wrathful face of an Asura,
Overshadowing the sun and moon with darkness.
One is the smiling and laughing face,
Watching over those who follow the commands with joy.
One is the wrathful Rakshasa face,
Eating the wicked enemies and obstructors as food.
One is the majestic devouring face,
Bringing down the great meteor of sky-iron fire.
One is the terrifying and wicked one,
Clapping together the sounds of heat and cold.
One is the wrathful face causing turmoil,
Bringing down the hail of great trembling.
One is the great fierce face of primordial wisdom,
With unimpeded clairvoyance and miraculous power.
One is the face of great strength and miracles,
Protecting the teaching of the Buddha.
One is the peaceful face of a god,
Granting accomplishments to the practitioner.
At the very top is the raven face,
Praising the high status of the Triple Gem.
With a sword and noose like lightning,
You cut the lineage of hateful enemies.
By swinging the crocodile noose,
You bring the three existences under your power.
By wielding the bow and arrow of Ra <note>Referring to the planet Rahu's weapon</note>,
You cut down the targeted enemies and obstructors from the root.
With the glaring eyes of a fire-mound,
You stare fixedly at enemies and obstructors.
By striking your lower body on the earth,
You cause the world to shake and tremble.
By shouting Hum and Phat from your mouths,
You bring the arrogant males and females under your power.
With a smoke-colored terrifying body...

ཡང་འདི་ལ་ལག་ལེན་གྱི་ཁྱད་པར་ནི། དབང་བཀའ་སྤྱི་ཙམ་ལ་ཐུན་མོང་དབང་བཞི་ཁོ་ནའི་མཐར་གཏོར་མི་བཀའ་གཏད་ཉིད་སྦྱོར་ཞིང་། རྐྱེན་སལ་གྱི་གཏོར་དབང་བྱེ་མ་བྱེད་ན། སྔོན་འགྲོ་གསོལ་བཏབ་དང་ཡན་ལག་བདུན་པ་རྩལ་བྱས་ནས། དངོས་གཞིའི་སྐབས་
གཏོར་མ་ལྟར་བསྐྱེད་པའི་དམིགས་པ་འཕོག་ནས། གཏོར་དབང་དང་བཀའ་སྒོ་སྔར་བཞིན་བྱ་བ་ལས་གཏོར་མའི་ལྷ་མི་བསྟིམ་ཡང་དེ་ཉིད་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་དུ་བྱེད་ན་སློབ་མ་ཡང་ལྷར་བསྐྱེད་ཅིང་གཏོར་མའི་ལྷ་ཡང་དཀྱུས་བཞིན་བསྟིམ་པའོ། །ཡང་གོང་གི་དབང་བཀའ་ཡོད་
རྫོགས་ཐུན་མོང་མིན་པའི་ལུགས་སུ་བསྐུར་ན་གྲྭ་ཚ་བོ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ལྷ་དབང་གི་རྗེས་སུ། དེའི་སྔགས་ཀྱི་བཟླས་ལུང་དང་། དེ་རྗེས་ལས་མཁན་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྐུའི་གཟུགས་གཏད་པའི་མཐར་དེ་དག་གི་སྔགས་ཀྱི་བཟླས་ལུང་སྦྱར་ནས་དྲེགས་པའི་སྲོག་ཡིས་སུ་བཞི་པ་དང་།
གཏོར་མའི་བཀའ་བསྒོའི་སྐབས་ལས་མགོན་གྱི་གཏོར་མ་ལག་ཏུ་གཏད་ནས་དམ་བསྲེས་པ་སོགས་གནད་རྣམས་ཤེས་པར་བྱའོ། །མི་འགྱུར་ཟག་མེད་ཡིས་ཀྱི། །རྣམ་རོལ་རྡོ་རྗེ་ནག་པོ་ཆེས། །ཡོངས་ཤར་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་དབང་གི་ཁྲིགས། །ཉུང་གསལ་འཇུག་པ་དེའི་
དཔྱིད་དུ་སྤེལ། །ཡེ་ཤེས་མགོན་པོ་ཕྱག་བཞི་པའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་དབང་དང་བཅས་པའི་ལེའུ་ཚན་ནོ།། །།
pages.translation: In short, one should abide by all the general and specific commitments. Then the student accepts this and offers the mandala fee, etc. For the conclusion, perform the thanksgiving offerings to the front-generation as known from the general sadhana. Furthermore, regarding the specific practical applications: for a general empowerment, simply attach the torma entrustment at the end of the four common empowerments. If performing the torma-empowerment separately for averting circumstances, first perform the preliminary request and the seven-limb prayer. During the main part, project the visualization of the generation of the torma, then perform the torma-empowerment and the command as before without dissolving the deities of the torma. If one wishes to make it even more special, the student is also generated as the deity and the torma deities are dissolved as usual. Also, if bestowing according to the uncommon tradition of the complete empowerment cycle, following the deity-empowerment of the Consort and the retinue <note>Gwa tsha bo</note>, perform the mantra-recitation transmission for them. Then, after handing over the physical forms of the action-workers, join it with their mantra-recitation transmissions. One should understand these key points, such as the fourth life-entrustment for the proud ones and the mixing of commitments while handing over the torma of the Action Protector during the command. Through the manifestation of the unchanging, untainted wisdom, the Black Vajra Mahakala, this condensed and clear arrangement of the sadhana and empowerment ritual was composed for the benefit of practitioners. This completes the chapter on the sadhana and empowerment of the Four-Armed Wisdom Protector.

"He seems to be coming! By all means, it is better to come!" they said, and placed me on a silk palanquin. They carried me through the sky like a bird flying. In the center of the gathering of those called the knowledge-holders and dakinis, like a lotus flower of deities, was a palace, vast and high. It was a skull-mansion without distinction between outer and inner. It had three tiers, and within radiated the light of great rainbows of various kinds. On a throne spread with a mandala on the upper floor, I saw the Vajra Dakini in the east, the Jewel Dakini in the south, the Lotus Dakini in the west, the Karma Dakini in the north, and the Buddha Dakini in the center. Surrounded by immeasurable retinues corresponding to each of the five families, they wore bone ornaments on their bodies. They sat sounding the <term>damaru</term> <gloss>hand-drum</gloss> and bell in their right and left hands. From among them, a woman wearing a red cloak stood up and said: "Kye! Knowledge-holder Pema Lingpa, it is good that you have come. Bestow an empowerment upon us vīras and dakinis!" I replied, "I have no ritual texts to bestow empowerment." Then, the woman in the center of the palace said: "Pema Lingpa, listen here! Establish the appearance-mind as the basis of the ritual text. Cut through the limits of words for whatever appearances arise. Demonstrate the realization of the meaning!"
<leaf-break/>
Then a person appeared and said, "Why have you all come here for my son? What is the purpose? He has not yet finished taking the treasures of the lower part of Bumthang and the three treasures of Chimphu Senge Dzong, and his work for the benefit of beings is not yet complete. Escort him back to his own land!" As soon as he said this, he struck everyone once with a whip he held in his hand. "Pema Lingpa, do not stay here! Go to your own land and spread my Dharma treasures to the sons who are worthy vessels through skillful means! It is fine even if no one in the world is pleased. Act so as not to contradict my heart!" Thus he spoke. I thought, "This must be my supreme father of Oddiyana." Thinking I must request a teaching, I said, "Please grant me one instruction on the definitive meaning." The Precious One of Oddiyana spoke: "Listen here, my son Pema Lingpa! The nature of all appearances and existence, samsara and nirvana, is the perfectly pure dharmakaya from the very beginning. Awareness is self-arisen and stainless. The self-arisen Buddha dwells within you. Since he dwells there, do not seek him elsewhere!" As soon as he spoke, the four women from before came again carrying the palanquin, and a sound arose from all the women in that palace.

He sat in the form of Vajradhara. I prostrated and requested his blessing. The one of Oddiyana spoke: "Stay here for the vase ritual!" While I was staying in his presence, Padmasambhava of Oddiyana stretched his right hand into the sky and pointed three fingers towards the heavens. I saw a tree growing from the tip of his thumb, its leaves and flowers beautiful. At the tip of his index finger, rainbow light swirled, and I saw various colors clearly. At the tip of his middle finger, I saw a stainless, round crystal vase. "Sole father, Padma, what do I understand these three signs to be?" In response to his speech, I replied: "The tree growing from the thumb with flourishing leaves and flowers is understood as the nirmanakaya. The swirling rainbow at the tip of the index finger with various clear colors is understood as the sambhogakaya. The stainless round crystal vase at the tip of the middle finger is understood as the great dharmakaya free from elaboration." དགའ་བཟང་མོ་ན་རེ། བླ་མ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་བདག་ལ་སྡོམ་ཆོག་དང་གསོལ་འདེབས་སྤེལ་མ་ཅིག་ཞུ་རྗེས་ཞུས་པས། འདི་གསུངས་སོ།། །།ན་མོ་གྷུ་རུ།། འགྲོ་བའི་དཔལ་མགོན་ཨྱན་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་སོ་བྱིན་གྱིས་རློབས།།སྤྲོས་པའི་རྟོག་པ་ཟང་ཙམ་ན།།ཡེ་ཤེས་སྣང་བ་ཤར་བ་དང།།སྐུ་གསུམ་དགོངས་པ་ལོན་པ་རུ།།གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་སོ་བྱིན་ཀྱིས
རློབས།།གདག་འབྲས་བུ་སྒྲུབ་པ་ལ།།སྒྲོན་བཞིའི་ལམ་ལ་རྩལ་སྦྱངས་ནས།།ཆོས་རྣམས་ཟང་སར་འཁྱོལ་བ་རུ།།གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་སོ་ཕྱིན་གྱིས་རློབས།།རྩ་བརྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་ཚོགས་རྣཾས
ལ།།གསོལ་བ་བཏབ་པའི་བྱིན་བརླབས་ཀྱིས།།ས་དང་ལམ་ལ་མ་ལྟོས་པར།།ཐར་པའི་ལམ་མཆོག་མྱུར་ཐོབ་ནས།།དོན་གཉིས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་བ་རུ།།གསོལ་བ་འདེབསོ་བྱིན་གྱིས
རློབས།།འཆི་ཁར་གནང་གཅོད་མེད་པ་དང།།དབའ་བོ་མཁའ་འགྲོས་མདུན་བསུ་ནས།།མཁའ་སྤྱོད་གནས་སུ་འཁྲིད་པ་རུ །།གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་སོ་བྱིནགྱིས་རློབས།།ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས
ལ་གནས་བྱས་ནས།།སྐུ་གསུམ་འབྲས་བུ་ཐོབ་ནས་ཀྱང།།ཀུན་བཟང་སྦས་ཀྱི་ཐུ་བོ་རུ།།གདོད་མའི་ས་ལ་འཁོད་པར་ཤོག།།ཅེས་གསུངསོ།། །།ཡང༑ ལུག་ལོ་ལ་མོན་ཡུལ་བསྡུར
ཞེས་བྱ་བར།།ཇོ་བོ་ཟླ་བ་འབུམ་གྱི་བསོན་དགེ་བཟང་པོ་བྱས་པའི་དུས། བླ་མ་ཀློང་ཡངས་རྒྱ་མཚོན་རེ། བདག་ལ་དྲི་མེད་པའི་མཚན་བརྒྱད་སོ་སོར་ཕྱེ་བའི་གསོལ་འདེབས་ཅིག་ཞུ་ཞུས་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །སྒོར་ཕྱེ་ནམ་མཁའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་བཏགས། །རླུང་སེམས་དབང་ཐོབ་དབུ་མའི་འདུད་པ་གྲོལ། །ནམ་མཁའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ཞབས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་འདེབས། །རྩེ་ཐང་གནྶ
གཞིར་ཡོན་ཏན་གྲགས་པ་རྒྱས། །ཕྱི་ནང་སྒྲུབ་མཐའ་ཀུན་ལ་ཐོགས་མེད་བྱུང། །སླཽན་དགྱེས་ནས་ཕན་པ་བཟང་པོར་བཏགས། །རྒྱལ་བའི་གདུང་འཛིན་བསྟན་པའི་སྲོག་ཤིང་འཛིན། །
ཕན་པ་བཟང་པོའི་ཞབས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་། །ལྷོ་བྲག་ཕྱོགས་ཕྱིན་གྷུ་རུ་ལྔ་ཁང་དུ། །འབྱུང་གནས་རྡོ་ཆོས་དབང་བརྒྱུད་དང་མཇལ། །བཀའ་བརྒྱད་ཡོངས་རྫོགས་རྒྱུད་སྡེ་མ་ལུས
ཀུན། །བླ་མ་དགྱེས་ནས་གུ་ཡངས་བློ་བདེར་བཏགས། །ཐོད་རྒལ་ཁྲེགས་(ཚོང་)འཁོར་འདས་གཞི་རྩ་བྲལ། །གུ་ཡངས་བློ་བདེའི་ཞབས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་འདེཔས། །སེ་བ་ལུང་དུ་རིན་ཆེན་གླིང་དང
མཇལ། །མཁའ་འགྲོ་སྙིང་ཐིག་གཉེན་པོ་ལྷ་གསུམ་ཐོབ། །ཨྱན་ལུང་(བ)སྟན་དྲི་མེད་འོད་ཟེར་གྲགས། །ཀུན་བཟངས་དགོངས་པ་འདུ་འབྲལ་མེད་པ་ཡི། །དྲི་མེད་འོད་ཟེར་ཞབས་ལ་གསོལ

Ornament and Protector of beings, to the learned and accomplished Drime Ozer <note>Dri med 'od zer, also known as Longchenpa</note>, I pray with devotion from the depths of my heart. May I never be separated from you. In the Palace of Dharma where you dwell, the prayers of the Guru have reached their end. Many doors to profound treasures have been opened. To Pema Lingpa, the glory who leads fortunate beings and expounds the Secret Mantra, I pray with devotion from the depths of my heart. Bless me that I may be taken under your care. Bless me that I may fulfill the intentions of the Father Guru. Bless me that I may never be separated from the Father. To the Precious One who has cared for me with kindness, I bow my crown to your lotus feet. Bless me that we may be non-dual. I pray that the Guru's health may be good. I pray that your life may be supremely long. I pray that your activities may flourish and expand. Bless me that I may never be separated from the Guru. Thus it was spoken.

Again, in the Year of the Monkey, while traveling through the three lower valleys of Mon, on the tenth day of the Month of the Dragon, the nun Kunga Zangmo said: "Precious Guru, please grant me a combined rite of vows and a prayer." Thereupon, he spoke this:

Homage to the Guru! The glorious protector of beings of Oddiyana...

<leaf-break/>

...I pray, grant your blessings. When the elaborations of thought are momentarily cleared, may the vision of primordial wisdom arise, and may I realize the intention of the Three Bodies <term>Trikaya</term>; I pray, grant your blessings. In accomplishing the ultimate result, having trained in the path of the Four Lamps <note>A practice in the Direct Crossing (Thogal) tradition</note>, may I reach the point where all phenomena are exhausted; I pray, grant your blessings. By the blessings of having prayed to the assembly of Root and Lineage Gurus, without depending on the levels <term>bhumi</term> and paths, may I quickly attain the supreme path of liberation and perfect the two goals <note>The welfare of oneself and others</note>; I pray, grant your blessings. At the time of death, may there be no painful transition, and being welcomed by the heroes <term>daka</term> and sky-goers <term>dakini</term>, may I be led to the celestial realms; I pray, grant your blessings. Having taken residence in the expanse of phenomena <term>dharmadhatu</term>, and having obtained the result of the Three Bodies, may I be established in the primordial ground as the eldest son of Samantabhadra <note>The Primordial Buddha</note>. Thus it was spoken.

Again, in the Year of the Sheep, at a place called Mon-yul Bedur, during the time of performing virtuous deeds for the late Lord Dawa Bum, the Guru Longyang Gyatso requested: "Please grant a prayer that distinguishes the eight names of Drime <note>Drime Ozer/Longchenpa</note> individually."

<leaf-break/>

The door was opened, and he was named the Yogi of Space. Having gained power over the winds and mind, the knots of the central channel were released. To the feet of the Yogi of Space <term>Namkhai Naljor</term>, I pray. At the seat of Tsethang, his fame for qualities flourished. In all philosophical systems, outer and inner, he was unimpeded. The teacher being pleased, he was named Phanpa Zangpo <gloss>Exalted Benefit</gloss>. Holding the lineage of the Victors, he is the life-pillar of the Teachings. To the feet of Phanpa Zangpo, I pray. Going toward the region of Lhodrak, in the Five-Room Temple of the Guru, he met the lineage of Nyangral Nyima Ozer and Guru Chowang. All the Eight Commands <term>Kagye</term> and the entire classes of Tantra without exception were received. The Guru being pleased, he was named Guyang Lode <gloss>Carefree Mind</gloss>. In the practices of Direct Crossing and Trekcho, the ground of cyclic existence and transcendence was severed. To the feet of Guyang Lode, I pray. In Sewalung, he met Rinchen Lingpa. He received the Heart Essence of the Dakinis <term>Khandro Nyingthig</term> and the three fierce deities. In accordance with the prophecy of Oddiyana, he became famous as Drime Ozer <gloss>Stainless Light</gloss>. To the feet of Drime Ozer, who is inseparable from the intention of Samantabhadra, I pray. Again, at the snowy enclosure of Yarlung Shampo, with the Great Knowledge-Holder Sumreza, he requested all the cycles and instructions of the Great Perfection <term>Dzogchen</term> without exception. The Knowledge-Holder being pleased, he was named Longchen Rabjam...

ནས་འཁྲུལ་མེད་ཡིན་ཀྱང། །འཁྲུལ་་་སམ་་་འཁྲུལ་བའི་ངོ་བོ། །བྱུངས་ཁུངས་རྩ་བ་ལྟོས་ཤིག། །གཉུགམ་སེམས་ཀྱི་གནད་ལུགས། །གདོད་ནས་བྱུང་ས

དང་གནས་བསམ་འཛིན་པ། །གནས་མཁན་ངོ་བོ་ལྟོས་ཤིག། གཉུག་མ་སེམས་ཀྱི་གནས་ལུགས ། །གདོད་ནས་འགྲོ་འོང་མེད་ཀྱང། །འགྲོ་དང་འགྲོ་བྱའི་རྟོག་པ

Salutations to the Guru! Padmasambhava, who knows the three times, and Pema Lingpa, stay as the ornament on the crown of my head. I, Pema Lingpa, a yogi of the evil age, though I have no provisional meaning, will show the definitive meaning for the benefit of others. Followers and students with good fortune, keep this in your minds without distraction. Though the natural mode of the innate mind has been unerring from the beginning, look at the root and source of the essence of delusion. Though the natural mode of the innate mind has had no place of arising from the beginning, look at the initial ground of the effort of arising and achieving. Though the natural mode of the innate mind has been without staying from the beginning, look at the essence of the one who stays and the grasping at the thought of staying. Though the natural mode of the innate mind has had no going or coming from the beginning, look at who it is that goes, the thought of going and the object of going. Though the natural mode of the innate mind has been empty from the beginning, look at whether the essence of appearance at the time of emptiness is pervasive or not.

<leaf-break/>

—not being primordial, cut the distance to the source of the delusion of afflictions! **TA**: having meditated on the stainless concentration, **THA**: realize the ultimate intention! **DA**: if you achieve the great goal, you hold your own ground. **NA**: stay in the meaning that is without error. **PA**: you will find immeasurable happiness. **PHA**: you will find the seven noble riches. Regarding that thought of coarse meditation, **MA**: it is exhausted in its own place of non-objectification. **TSA**: with precise and detailed diligence and effort, **TSHA**: whatever elaborations of words and meanings arise, **DZA**: without falling under the power of grasping, **WA**: do not leave it in a daze, but look at the mind. **ZHA**: rest calmly in the state of <term>shamatha</term> <gloss>calm abiding</gloss>. **ZA**: when grasping with defilement is exhausted at this time, **'A**: <term>vipashyana</term> <gloss>insight</gloss> luminosity will arise from within. **YA**: the innate meaning without movement or agitation. **RA**: having found it in yourself, recognize your own nature. **LA**: the excellent fruit is already achieved. **SHA**: the joyful realm of the basic space of phenomena. **SA**: residing on the level of Buddha. **A**: from the state of the unborn <term>dharmakaya</term>, **HA**: it is not a mere daze, but—

<leaf-break/>

—mother, son, and relatives are prompted by their own respective karma. When death occurs in succession, if I take on the suffering of others, who will take on the suffering of my own death? When the benefit of karma is exhausted, even the Buddhas of the three times must depart when their work for beings is finished. What power to stay do any of the sentient beings of the three realms have? When the time comes to be struck by the demon of the Lord of Death, even if one is a universal monarch, one must depart, leaving the kingdom behind. Even the lines of lords and provincial leaders must depart, abandoning their forts and estates. Even wealthy householders must depart, leaving their wealth and goods behind. Even without children or relatives, each must go alone. Just as others have departed before for the sake of others, there is no certainty when it will come for oneself. Keep that in mind and abandon current activities! There is no benefit in having done them. To this worldly stream of Dharma, like the ripples on flowing water—

Homage to the Guru! May a person like me, who is weary of the dull-witted cyclic existence, having entered the path of the Great Vehicle and pursued the path of liberation, have as my sole refuge for achieving Buddhahood in this life the supreme guide, the Lord of Victors, Padmasambhava. Having arrived in the sky before me, please be the witness for the accomplishment of this pure aspiration. By the power of deep karmic connections from the past, I have offered my heart and three gates to the Heart-Son of Orgyen, Pema Lingpa. With your compassionate hook of guidance, I pray that you lead me to the path of liberation right now from the ocean of afflicted cyclic existence. Even if it costs my life, for the sake of taking the essence of this precious human body, I will practice the essential meaning of the profound treasures of Orgyen, the heart-essence of Pema Lingpa. Having bound the demonic ego-grasping within the mind's faults, may the natural state of the awareness of emptiness be realized. Having perfected the power of awareness of all of appearance and existence, cyclic existence and transcendence, may the effort of achieving the path be exhausted, and at the end of the exhaustion of phenomena—
<leaf-break/>
All sentient beings of the three <note>realms</note>, by the great equanimity without near or far, without leaving any behind as near or far in future times, may they attain liberation right now.

Whatever aspirations the Buddhas of the five families made, may I accomplish them all. Whatever aspirations the Powerful Hero made, may I accomplish them all. Whatever aspirations Vajra-Dharma made, I <note>accomplish</note> them all. Whatever aspirations Manjushri made, I <note>accomplish</note> them all. Whatever aspirations Avalokiteshvara made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations the Lord of Secrets Vajrapani made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Garab Dorje made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Shri Singha made, those <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Orgyen Padma made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Manjushrimitra made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Humkara made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Nagarjuna made, they all <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Dhana-Sanskrita made, those <note>are accomplished</note>. Whatever aspirations Nyima Mitra made, those <note>are accomplished</note>.
<leaf-break/>
The ten virtues and the five crimes of immediate retribution, may all bad karma and obscurations without exception be abandoned and purified right now. Whatever aspirations the Victors of the three times made, I <note>will accomplish</note> them all. May their compassionate blessings enter me, and may demons, obstacle-makers, interferers, and spirits; diseases, epidemics, poisons, and weapons; famine, enemies, thieves, and all collections of inauspiciousness be absent from wherever I reside. Whatever aspirations the Victors of the three times made, having accomplished them all, may their compassionate blessings enter me. May the conditions of untimely death be pacified, and may my life be extended to a hundred years. མེད་པ་དེ་ངེས་ཤེས་ལྷང་གིས་སྐྱེས་ནས་གཞན་སྣང་ལ་མཁའགྲོ་མས་སྐོར་བ་འཾ། ལུས་དུ་མར་མཐོང་པའཾ། མོུས་ཅན་གྱི་རྟེན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་ལ་སདྱས་རང་གི་སྣང་བར་ཤར་ནས་ཀྱང་འོང་། ངག་
ཅི་སྨྲས་པ་ཐཾད་ཆོས་སུ་ཡང་འགྲོ། ལུས་སྤྱོད་པ་ཅི་བྱས་ཀྱང་སེཾན་དད་ནུས། གནས་གར་བསྡད་ཀྱི་བྱིན་རླབས་སྐྱེ་། གྲོཌ་མེདར་༡་པུར་བསྡད་ཀྱང་ལུང་པ་གང་ཕྱིན་པ་ཐཾད་དུ་འཇིཌ་པ་མེད་།
རེས་བྱིས་པའི་སྤྱོད་པ་བྱེད་། རེས་འཇྟིེན་འདི་ལ་དགའ་སྙམ་པའི་བསམ་པ་ཡང་གཞན་ལ་འོང་། དོན་ མདོར་བསྡུ་ན་བྱང་སེཾས་༢་དང་མ་བྲལ་བའོ་། ཕྱིར་བསྒོམ་མེད་མཐར་ཕྱིན་པ་
ལ་སེཾན་ལ་སྙིངེ་རང་ཤུཌ་ཀྱིས་སྐྱེ་། ལས་རྒྱུ་འབྲས་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་འགྱུར་། ཚིག་ཐཾད་སྐྱེ་མེད་ཀྱི་དོན་དུ་སྟོན་། གང་ལ་ཡང་ཞེན་པ་མེད་། གཙང་ཙོགི་རྣཾར་རྟོག་པ་ཆུང་

ལོན་པ། དེ་ལྟར་མ་རྟོགས་པའི་སེཾན་ལ་སྙིངེ་ རང་ཤུགསཾ་ངང་གིས་འོང་པས་ཅི་བྱེད་པ་སེཾན་གྱི་དོན་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་། དེ་ལྟུ་དྲུག་དང་ལྡན་པའི་ལམ་འདི་སྐབས་བརྒྱད་དེ་། སྒྲུབ་པ་པོའི་ལག་
ཆར་ཁྱེར་བས་ཕྱིར་མི་ལྡོག་པའི་ས་ཐོབ་སྟེ་། སེམས་དང་རྟོག་པ་ཐ་མི་དད་ཅིང་ཐཾད་སྐུ་བཞིར་ཁྱེར་བས་རྣམ་པ་ཐཾད་མཁྱེན་པ་ལམ་དུ་ཤེས་པས་ལམ་ཤེས་བསྒྲུབ་པ་པོ་ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་ནས་བར་བྱས་པ་
མ་ཡིན་ཏེ་། གདོད་མ་ཉིད་ནས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་དེ་ལྟར་ཡིན་པས་གཞིར་ཤེས་པ་། རྒྱུ་ལམ་འབྲས་བུ་གསུམ་ངོ་བོ་ཅིག་ཏུ་བྱུང་པས་རྣམས་ཀུན་མངོན་སྫོགས་། དེ་ལྟར་
<leaf-break/>
བྱས། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་གྲོགས་བྱས། དེ་གསུམ་ནི་ཐབས་ཡིན། དེ་ཤེས་པས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་རྟེན་འབྲེལ་སྐྲུན་པས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དུ་འབྱུང་བས་འབྲས་བུ། དེ་ལྟར་དབང་པོ་ལྔ་ལག་
ཏུ་བླངས་པས་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རྩལ་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་འབྱོངས་པ་ལ་ཚེག་མེད་པས་སྟོབས་ལྔ། དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་རྟེན་འབྲེལ་སྒྲུན། ཐབས་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རྩལ་འབྱོངས། དེ་ལས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་
སེམས་སྐྱེ་བས། དྲན་རིག་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་ཀྱི་གྲོགས་སུ་འགྱུར་བས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་གོ། ཐམས་ཅད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་ཏུ་ཤེས་པས་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ཀྱང་རྣམ་རྟོག་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མི་གཡོ་བས།
དེ་ཉིད་ལམ་དུ་འགྲོ་བས་འཕགས་པའི་ལམ་ཡན་ལག་བརྒྱད་པའོ། དེ་ཉིད་ལམ་དང་། དེ་ལྟར་ལྟ་བའི་གོ་ཆས་བརྡར་ཤ་གཅད་ནས་གོལ་ས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་མཐའ་ཁེགས་ནས། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་གོ་ཆས་
རྟོག་པ་ལམ་དུ་འཁྱེར་བའི་དུས་སུ། གོང་དུ་བསྟན་པའི་ལམ་གྱི་ཡན་ལག་གིས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྔོ་བགྲང་བྱེད་དམ་ཞེ་ན། བྱས་ན་སྐྱོན་དུ་འགྲོ་སྟེ། ལམ་འདི་ནི་བསྒོམ་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་
འབའ་ཞིག་ལ་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན། བསྒོམ་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ནི་ཚིག་དང་བློ་ལས་འདས་པ་ཡིན། འོ་ན་ལམ་དུ་ཇྟིར་ཁྱེར་ཞེ་ན། དྲན་པ་ལམ་དུ་འཁྱེར་ཏེ། གང་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་འཁྱེར་ཞེ་ན།
<leaf-break/>
ལ་དེ་ལ་བྱ་ ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་རྟོག་པའི་རྩ་བ་ངོ་ཤེས་པས་མཐའ་དང་བྲལ་བས་དབུ་མ་ཞེས་ཀྱང་དེ་ལ་བྱའོ་། ཉཽངས་བག་ལ་ཞ་བར་འགྱུར་། བཤེས་གཉེན་དམ་པས་གསུངས་པ་
རྣམས་། གུས་པའི་ཡིད་ཀྱིས་ཡི་གེར་བཀོད་། སྒྲོ་བསྐུར་དྲིན་དུ་མི་གཟོ་ལ་། ཡི་གེ་སྤེལ་བར་མི་བྱ་གསུང་། བླ་མ་མཉམ་མེད་རོིེན་། གདམས་པ་ཁྱད་འཕགས་
ཕྱག་དྱ་ཆེ་། བཤཻན་མྱང་ལ་གདམས་པ་འདི་། སེཾན་ཀུན་གྱིས་ཐོབ་པར་ཤོག། ཨིཐཱིཿ །། ཉེས་པ་མ་ལུས་སྐྱོབས་བྱེད་བླ་མ་དང་། འཁོར་ལོ་སྡོམ་
པའི་ཞབས་ལ་གུས་པས་འདུད་། ཚེ་འདི་ཉིད་ལ་ལྟོས་ཐག་བཅད་ནས་བསྒྲུབ་པ་བྱེད་པ་ལ་། སྤང་བྱ་དང། བླང་བྱ་གཉིས། སྤང་བྱ་ནི། རྒྱུའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་ཞེན་། བདག་པོའི་
རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་ལོག་པའི་བཤཻན་དང་ཕྲད་། དམིགས་པའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་འཁྲུལ་། དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་རེ་དོགས་སུ་ཤོར་བ་ལས་འཁོར་བར་སྣང་། བླང་བྱ་ནི། རྒྱུའི་རྐྱེན་གྱི་དུས་
ན་མ་ཞེན་། བདག་པོའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་ཡང་དག་པའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་ཕྲད་། དམིཌ་པའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་མ་འཁྲུལ་། དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་སྐྱོན་གྱིས་དུས་ན་རེ་དོགས་མེད་པ་རང་སེམས་

One understands the mind to be like the Buddha; there is nothing to be abandoned, and no remedy to rely on. One is free from something to do and free from the "doing mind." One gains a deep certainty thinking "there is no death or non-death." When that certainty of the lack of distinction between meditation and post-meditation arises vividly, in the perception of others, one may be surrounded by <term>dakinis</term> <gloss>sky-goers</gloss> or seen in multiple bodies. To a person of devotion, the Buddha may even appear in their own perception. Whatever words are spoken become Dharma. Whatever physical actions are done can inspire faith in sentient beings. Wherever one stays, blessings arise. Even staying alone without companions, one is fearless wherever one goes. Sometimes one acts like a child. Others may think "He is fond of this world." In short, it is never being separate from the two <term>bodhicittas</term> <gloss>relative and absolute awakened mind</gloss>. Furthermore, at the culmination of non-meditation, compassion for sentient beings arises naturally. The cause and effect of karma become evident. All words teach the meaning of birthlessness. One has no attachment to anything. Discursive thoughts about pure and impure are small. In the secret place, the thought arises that there is no need for shame. All heroes and dakinis make offerings and assist in benefiting sentient beings. One thinks, "I am delayed only by one birth"...

<leaf-break/>

That "Abbot" <note>Khenpo</note> is the wisdom that arises from ungrounded awareness and is unobstructed; that is the Sangha. On that special path, whatever thoughts arise become the path of the six perfections: those very thoughts provide the impulse and act as assistants. By knowing the characteristic of the thoughts themselves, it is Wisdom. By taking all thoughts as the path, it is Concentration. By perfectly training in that very path whenever a thought arises, it is Diligence. By not being afraid of the meaning of reality, it is Patience. Because there are no seeds of affliction in such a meaning, it is Stainless Ethics. Having taken into hand the dependent origination of such Method and Wisdom; because compassion for sentient beings who have not realized this arises naturally, whatever one does becomes for the benefit of beings, which is Generosity. This path possessing those six is the "Eight Stages"; by carrying them as the practitioner's tools, one obtains the level of non-returning. Mind and thoughts are inseparable, and by taking all as the four bodies, one knows Omniscience on the path. This is not something newly created by the practitioner being skilled in means. Since the very beginning, the characteristic of Emptiness has been so; thus, it is Knowledge of the Ground. Because the cause, path, and result arise as one essence, it is the Manifest Perfection of all Aspects. Thus...

<leaf-break/>

...was done. Diligence acted as the assistant. Those three are the Method. By knowing that, the dependent origination of wisdom is established; since everything arises in meditative absorption, it is the Result. Thus, by taking the five faculties into hand, the power of wisdom and the training in <term>bodhicitta</term> are effortless; these are the five powers. Thus, the dependent origination of wisdom is established and the power of method and wisdom is refined. From that, bodhicitta is born. Since all mindfulness and awareness become assistants to bodhicitta, they are the branches of enlightenment. By knowing everything as a branch of bodhicitta, even while enjoying everything, discursive thoughts do not waver. Because that itself proceeds as the path, it is the Noble Eightfold Path. That itself is the path. Once the view is decided by the armor of the view and all extremes of error are blocked, at the time of carrying thoughts on the path through the armor of wisdom, one might ask if the branches of the path shown above are counted as the numbers of wisdom. If one does so, it becomes a fault. This path is used only for the wisdom of meditation. The wisdom of meditation is beyond words and the conceptual mind. Then, how is it carried on the path? Mindfulness is carried on the path. Upon what does it rely to be carried?

<leaf-break/>

...should be done. Because one recognizes the root of the thoughts of wisdom, it is free from extremes, so it is also called the "Middle Way" <note>Madhyamaka</note>. Afflictive tendencies will be diminished. These things spoken by the holy spiritual friend were put into writing with a devoted mind. He said: "Do not be ungrateful for the kindness of the instructions, and do not distribute this writing." The peerless precious Guru, the supreme instruction of Mahamudra: may this instruction for Shennyen Nyang be obtained by all sentient beings. <term>Iti</term> <gloss>thus it ends</gloss>. I bow with devotion to the Guru who protects from all faults without exception, and to the feet of Chakrasamvara. For those who cut the ties of attachment to this life and practice: there are things to be abandoned and things to be taken up. Things to be abandoned: at the time of the causal condition, one is attached. At the time of the dominant condition, one meets a false friend. At the time of the objective condition, one is deluded. At the time of the immediate condition, one falls into hope and fear, and thus samsara appears. Things to be taken up: at the time of the causal condition, one is unattached. At the time of the dominant condition, one meets an authentic spiritual friend. At the time of the objective condition, one is undeluded. At the time of the immediate condition, one is without hope and fear for one's own mind...

༄༅༅།། བླ་མ་དམ་པ་རྣམས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ།། ཕྱག་དྱ་ཆེན་པོ་གཉུག་མ་ཆིག་ཆོད་འདི་ལ། དང་པོ་དམིགས་པ་འཛིན་པའི་
དུས་དང་གཅིག། བར་དུ་ངེས་ཤེས་སྐྱེས་པའི་དུས་དང་གཉིས། ཐ་མ་རྟོགས་པ་ཐོས་པའི་དུས་དང་གསུམ། དེའི་དོན་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བའི་དུས་དང་བཞིའོ།། དེ་
ལ་དང་པོ་དམིགས་པ་འཛིན་པ་དུས་ན། བསྒོམ་བཏབ་ནས་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པའི་དུས་སུ། སེམས་མ་བཅོས་མ་སྒྲིམ་པར། རང་སར་གློད་ནས་བཞག་
<leaf-break/>
ཀྱང་དེ་ལ་སེམས་མ་བཅོས་པ་། མ་སླད་པ། གཉུག་མའི་ངོ་བོ་དེ་ལ་ཟེར་བ་ཡིན་། དེའི་ངོ་བོ་ལ་སྐད་ཅིག་མ་ཅིག་ཀྱང་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡིན་ནོ་། སྐད་ཅིག་མ་༢་
སམ། ཟན་ཁམ་ཅིག་ཟ་ཡུན་ནམ། བ་འཇོ་བའི་ཡུན་ཙམ་གནས་ཀྱང་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡིན་། དེ་ལྟར་བསྒོམ་པའི་དུས་སུ། ཚོགས་དྲུག་ཡུལ་ལ་ཡེངས་སུ་མེད་། རིག་

པ་ནི། བསྒོམ་པའི་དུས་སུ་གཟུགས། སྒྲ། དྲི་རོ། རེག་བྱ་རྣམ་ཤེས་ཚོགས་དྲུགི་ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཡེངས། ཕྱེད་དུ་མ་ལྟོས་པས། མ་བཅོས་པའི་ཤེས་པ་

<leaf-break/>

Homage to the holy Gurus. In this "Single Sufficiency of the Co-emergent Great Mudra <term>Mahamudra</term>," there are: first, the time of holding the focus; second, the time when certain knowledge is born; third, the time when realization is heard; and fourth, the time when its meaning is experienced.
Regarding the first, the time of holding the focus: When one has begun meditation and is practicing, without altering or tightening the mind, let it rest relaxed in its own place...

<leaf-break/>

...That is called the "unaltered mind." Unpolluted. It refers to that co-emergent essence. Even for a single moment, its essence is the Truth Body <note>original: "Dharmakaya"</note>. Whether it remains for two moments, or for the duration of eating a mouthful of food, or for the duration of milking a cow, it is the Truth Body. At the time of meditating thus, there is no distraction of the six groups <note>the senses</note> toward objects. Awareness is held with diligence. One-pointedly, one aims and strikes. The conducive condition of diligence is very important. Furthermore, "no distraction of the six groups toward objects" means that at the time of meditation, one is not distracted by any of the objects of the six consciousnesses—form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects. By not looking dualistically, one is not distracted by anything other than that vivid, non-conceptual, unaltered consciousness. "Holding awareness with diligence" means this flickering and moving consciousness of the ground-of-all <term>alayavijnana</term> is like a spectacle...

<leaf-break/>

...If it is accomplished as a side-effect of what is called meditation, that is good. But if it is not accomplished, the type that just leaves it be has no name of "conducive condition." That is called the "first time of holding the focus." By meditating in that way, in the middle, a special certain knowledge is born. If you wonder how it is born: By experiencing the essence of the mind, which is the essence of awareness, vivid and non-conceptual, just as it is, one thinks: "Oh, the essence of the mind is like this! There is no way to make it exist, and there is no way to make it not exist. It exists as spontaneously present from the very beginning. Even if the teacher had not shown this, I would recognize it. It is so plain!" such a thought will arise. At that time, the mind does not stray to external objects. Grasping remains as mere self-clarity. Thus it is said. Its name is "the meditative absorption of continuous mindfulness." In meaning, it is what is called "having nothing to do because of resting in one's own place." "Not letting the mind go to external objects" means that at that time, appearances neither help nor harm you. Whether it is white, it is white; whether it is black, it is black—thinking thus, a state of not letting the mind go toward appearances will arise. Then, grasping...

<leaf-break/>

...There is no rejection or establishment. Whatever appears dawns as its own essence. The anticipation of both hope and fear is destroyed. The six groups <note>of senses</note> are naturally purified. Thus it is said. It means there is no rejection or establishment of both body and mind. One comes to realize the indivisibility of the external grasped object and the internal grasping mind. "Whatever appears dawns as its own essence" means that all phenomena of sound and appearance dawn as the essence of one's own mind, and it refers to not transcending that meaning. "The anticipation of both hope and fear is destroyed" means that one does not harbor fear of the lower cyclic existence and one does not harbor hope for the higher state of Buddhahood. "The six groups are naturally purified" means that all forms seen by the eye are known as non-conceptual in their own self-clarity and nature. Likewise, hearing sounds with the ear, experiencing with the tongue, smooth and rough touch of the body, and all memories and conceptual thoughts of the mind are known as non-conceptual in the nature of self-awareness. That is called the "natural purification of the six groups." That is called the "final time of obtaining realization." When such a realization is suddenly obtained, following it, this kind of experience...
